article_sentences: A Public Interest Litigation filed in the Supreme Court on September 25, 2026, by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi has brought an unprecedented internal rift within the Election Commission of India into the judicial spotlight.

It seeks the initiation of criminal proceedings against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, as well as a probe into the alleged unilateral orders of the CEC by forming a Special Investigation Team.

As per Indian Express expose, fourteen formal written objections to the Chief Election Commissioner's executive orders by the Election Commissioners Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Dr. Vivek Joshi were documented over a period of ten months, which cannot be dismissed as routine administrative friction.

The internal breach regarding the Chief Election Commissioner's unilateral executive orders without collective decision-making, the modification of voter registration rules via updates to digital portals, and the centralization of electoral rolls management in Delhi represent direct violations of multi-member decision-making obligations per the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

The Election Commission's official defense, issued on September 23, 2026, and reiterated following an all-member meeting on September 26, 2026, that written notes merely reflect standard internal deliberation fails statutory scrutiny.
In T.N. Seshan.

Union of India, the Supreme Court unambiguously denied the possibility of the existence of a supreme Chief Election Commissioner, as the statutory scheme was purposefully devised to prevent arbitrary executive governance.

The statutory framework governing the internal decision-making process is established in Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.

article_sentences: Congress workers staged a protest rally in Hubballi on October 11, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral malpractice and attempts to undermine democracy.

The rally was organised by the Vidyanagar and Unkal block Congress committees under the leadership of Rajat Ullagaddimath, Chairperson of the Hubballi-Dharwad City District Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority.
It began at Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Circle, where the protesters read out Article 326 of the Constitution, which provides for elections based on adult suffrage.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Ullagaddimath alleged that the RSS is conspiring to deprive oppressed and marginalised communities of their right to vote.
Describing the struggle to protect democracy and the Constitution as a ‘second freedom struggle’ against what he termed fascist forces, he called for concerted action to safeguard electoral rights.

Hundreds of Congress workers accused the BJP-led Union Government of attempting to manipulate the votes of Other Backward Classes, Economically Weaker Sections, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and minority communities.
They raised slogans against the Centre and demanded Mr. Kumar’s resignation.
Tension prevailed when the rally reached the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation office.
Protesters allegedly attempted to burn portraits of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Mr. Kumar, triggering a scuffle between the police and the demonstrators.
The police, subsequently, detained several protesters.

Hubballi-Dharwad District Congress president Sadanand Danganavar, I.G. Sanadi, KPCC member Satish Meharwade, Shahzaman Mujahid, Anwar Mudgol, Mohammed Sharif Gargad, and several councillors and party functionaries participated in the protest.

article_sentences: India's opposition parties are set to march to the Supreme Court in Delhi to demand the resignation of the election chief over alleged voter fraud.
This will be the latest in a series of demonstrations in Delhi, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital.
Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janata Party pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained.
Opposition parties allege that under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, India's voter rolls are being manipulated to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Both the Election Commission and the BJP have rejected the charge.
The opposition lawmakers want to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant, but he has told reporters he declined the meeting citing "certain reasons".
He did not provide the reasons, but media reports citing the letter have said that he pointed out that some of the issues the opposition wanted to raise with him were also pending before the court.
The BBC has not seen the letter.
"Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law," he told reporters.
Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, has called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march.

In a press conference on Monday, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to the Chief Justice, laying out their concerns with Kumar's alleged conduct and with the contentious electoral roll revision.
He said that Kant had asked them to file a petition, which they would do at the end of their march.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday clarified that it had not adjudicated on the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) modified Form 6 declaration for new voter registration, observing that the revised form was not before it when it decided the Bihar Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls case.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday clarified that it had not adjudicated on the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) modified Form 6 declaration for new voter registration, observing that the revised form was not before it when it decided the Bihar Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls case.

A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the clarification while hearing a fresh petition raising concerns over the functioning of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the changes to Form 6, which requires applicants seeking registration as new voters to disclose whether they or their parents were mapped in the previous SIR.

During the hearing, counsel for the petitioner submitted that the Supreme Court had clarified on October 5 that the modified Form 6 had not been approved by it, while the ECI had claimed that the revised declaration had received the top court’s approval.

Responding to the submission, Justice Bagchi said the Supreme Court had not adjudicated on the new Form 6, adding that the revised form was not in existence when the judgment in the Bihar SIR case was delivered.
"There is no adjudication on the new Form 6," he observed, clarifying that the apex court’s earlier oral remarks could not be construed as either approving or disapproving the modified declaration.
CJI Surya Kant cautioned against selectively interpreting the top court’s observations for media reports, saying: "Please don’t pick words for news items."

The clarification comes amid a political row over the modified Form 6 declaration, with questions being raised about the circumstances in which the changes were introduced and whether they were implemented despite objections from two Election Commissioners.

The controversy intensified after the ECI issued a press release on September 26 suggesting that the Supreme Court had upheld the revised declaration in its May 2026 judgment concerning the Bihar SIR exercise.
However, the modified declaration was introduced after the judgment, and the Supreme Court had no occasion to examine its contents while deciding the Bihar SIR matter.
Under the revised declaration, applicants seeking registration as new voters are required to state whether they or their parents were included in the previous SIR.
The earlier version of Form 6 used during the SIR exercise in other states did not contain this requirement.

stories.title: Jantar Mantar de-notified as protest site; Delhi Police designates 3 new venues
stories.summary: New Delhi , Oct 12 : Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a designated venue for organising protests and demonstrations in Delhi, with the Delhi Police designating three new locations for the purpose, according to an official notice. The three new designated protest venues are Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to examine alternative venues for citizens to exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations in place of the existing designated site. Based on the committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a protest venue, the notice stated. Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar said that a detailed and revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for organising protests and demonstrations at the three designated venues would be issued separately. The notice partially modifies the earlier Standing Order dated April 28, 2022. The revised SOP is expected to lay down the procedures for organising protests and demonstrations at the newly designated venues. The development comes as leaders and parliamentarians of the opposition INDIA bloc launched a massive protest march from Connaught Place in central Delhi, intensifying their agitation against the Election Commission over alleged electoral manipulation and subversion of democratic institutions. Launching a fierce attack on the central government during the march, Congress General Secretary (Organisation) KC Venugopal described the Opposition's ongoing agitation as the "biggest andolan" against the poll panel and declared that the party is taking its legal battle to the apex court. "This is the biggest andolan against the Election Commissioner and the election system. Narendra Modi and Amit Shah are using the Chief Election Commissioner as their tool to destroy the democracy of this country, to hijack the democracy of the country," Venugopal said. Emphasizing that the Opposition will fight on both political and legal fronts, he said, "Therefore, for the last one week, we are on the streets. Today also we are going to be on the streets, and we are going to file a petition in the Supreme Court also." When asked by reporters regarding an appointment with the Chief Justice of India, Venugopal stated, "I don't want to comment on all that now. But anyway, we are going to fight legally also. We are going to the Supreme Court and file a petition there. The Supreme Court, Chief Justice informed us that between 10:00 to 4:00, they are ready to receive our petition; the registry is ready." Joining the protest, Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury condemned the police clampdown and accused the government of acting with impunity despite judicial safeguards. "This is a show of giving them assurance that we are going to fight for them, that we represent them and their voice should be heard here. This brute force here and declaring us unlawful is a clear show of violation of anything that is constitutional and disrespect to the Supreme Court which this government is showing," Chowdhury said. She added, "Despite the Supreme Court's rulings, they have violated and they have named us. You ask about SIR and they filed an FIR. One Gyanesh is more than 'Bharat desh'?" Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee said, "We are demanding justice, nothing else. This is for people, for humankind, for justice...We want justice and nothing else." Against this backdrop, high security is in place in Central Delhi with barricades at multiple locations. Entry and exit at certain metro stations will also remain closed from 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM on October 12, 2026, for security reasons. The stations are Patel Chowk, Janpath, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Central Secretariat, Barakhamba Road respectively. Security personnel have been deployed at Barakhamba Road, near Mandi House. RAF (Rapid Action Force) and CRPF (Central Reserve Police Force) personnel are also deployed along with Delhi Police personnel.

stories.summary: The Gyanesh Kumar-led Election Commission of India, emboldened by a deferential Supreme Court judgment, has already disenfranchised lakhs of genuine electors through its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and risks excluding many more

article_sentences: For more than 75 years, the defining preoccupation of the Election Commission of India (ECI) has been “inclusion”.
The first general election of 1951-52 had to enrol an electorate of around 17 crore from scratch, many of whom were illiterate.
Successive Commissioners treated universal adult franchise as a promise to be fulfilled rather than just a principle to be stated on paper.
India could genuinely be proud of being an electoral democracy where voter turnout among the poor is higher than that among the rich, unlike in many western democracies.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls launched by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India, Gyanesh Kumar, has reversed this progressive direction.

It was termed an exercise to “purify” the electoral rolls, but in practice, it is riddled with methodological flaws and ad hoc rule changes, resulting in the deletion of a large number of genuine voters.
The names of 13.37 crore people were struck off during the draft stage across 30 States and Union Territories in the three phases of the SIR.
The figure includes 65 lakh in Bihar, 6.57 crore in the 12 States and Union Territories covered in Phase 2, and 6.15 crore in Phase 3, whose final rolls are yet to be published.
The deletion rate doubled as SIR progressed — from 8.3% in Bihar to 12.9% in Phase 2 and 17% in Phase 3 (it was 32.8% in Delhi and 21.7% in Telangana).
In Phases 1 and 2, even after names were added back, net deletions were about 6.2 crore.
In Delhi, the draft roll has only 97.54 lakh electors, barely above the 94.95 lakh who voted in the February 2025 Assembly election.
In 24 of Delhi’s 70 constituencies, the draft roll now has fewer electors than the number who voted in the election.

stories.title: "Environmental Protection Not Just Govt's Job, Citizens Equally Responsible": CM Omar
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 12 : Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Monday said environmental protection cannot be the government's responsibility alone and called for collective public participation, even as he cautioned against any abrupt curbs on tourism that sustains thousands of families in the region. Speaking at the J&K Agriculture Science Congress 2026 at Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), CM Omar Abdullah said the Union Territory was already facing the consequences of climate change, marked by erratic snowfall, water scarcity, landslides and floods. He said snowfall has become increasingly irregular, with insufficient winter precipitation hitting water availability in the following months. People face shortages in March, April and May, he said, only to see heavy rain and rising river levels later, triggering flood and landslide risks. This is our new reality. This is the reality we are living with," CM Omar said, stressing the need to sustain livelihoods while pursuing development. The Chief Minister said climate change cannot be fought by any single region or country in isolation and demands coordinated global action, while local communities must own the responsibility of protecting their surroundings and natural resources. On tourism, CM Omar said its environmental footprint must be addressed without disregarding the livelihoods of those dependent on the sector. He warned against suddenly restricting tourist arrivals, noting that tourism is the mainstay of many local families and businesses, and said any regulation of visitor numbers would have to be gradual and balanced. While conceding that tourism exerts pressure on the environment, he said tourists and vehicles alone cannot be blamed for pollution, plastic waste and water scarcity. He asked whether areas with negligible tourist activity were free of garbage and plastic pollution, and urged residents to look inward at their own practices. CM Omar came down heavily on the habit of throwing waste from vehicles and public transport, saying citizens must stop littering and take greater ownership of keeping their surroundings clean. He also urged people to cut down on single-use plastic bags by carrying reusable bags while shopping. Underlining the need for resource conservation, he asked people to avoid wasting water and to switch off lights, fans and heaters when not in use. The Chief Minister said that while the government has the primary responsibility for environmental protection, real change will come only through active public participation, and that sustainability and conservation can be achieved only when official action is matched by responsible citizen behaviour. (KNS).

article_sentences: The shutdown call comes amid fresh Kuki-Naga clashes that killed nine people in Manipur’s hill districts.

Imphal: Seven banned insurgent groups in Manipur have called for a statewide shutdown on October 15 to mark what they describe as “National Black Day”, protesting the state’s merger with the Indian Union in 1949.

The shutdown call comes amid renewed violence in Manipur’s hill districts, where nine people were killed in a fresh round of clashes involving members of the Kuki and Naga communities on Friday and Saturday.
The Coordination Committee (CorCom), an umbrella organisation comprising six banned underground outfits, has announced a 12-hour shutdown from 6 am to 6 pm on October 15.

The groups are the Kangleipak Communist Party (KCP), Kanglei Yawol Kanna Lup (KYKL), People’s Revolutionary Party of Kangleipak (PREPAK), PREPAK-Pro, Revolutionary People’s Front (RPF) and United National Liberation Front (UNLF).
The Socialist Revolutionary Party (SOREPA), which is not part of the six-member coalition, has separately called for a 12-hour shutdown from 5 am to 5 pm on the same day.
Both organisations have said essential services, including medical emergencies, media operations and religious activities, will be exempted.
Why are the groups protesting?
In separate statements, CorCom and SOREPA said October 15 is observed annually to protest Manipur’s merger with India.
Referring to the state by its former name, Kangleipak, the outfits alleged that the merger violated international and domestic legal provisions.

They cited Article 2(4) of the United Nations Charter, the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, the Manipur State Constitution Act, 1947, and the Indian Independence Act, 1947, in support of their claims.

The groups also alleged that the then ruler, King Bodhchandra, was pressured into signing the Manipur Merger Agreement in Shillong on September 21, 1949, claiming he was under house arrest and at gunpoint.
